rows.source: CAA loss-of-control-in-flight prevention
rows.verified: CAA identifies loss of control in flight as a major general-aviation safety issue.

rows.source: CAA loss-of-control-in-flight prevention
rows.verified: From 2018 to 2025, loss-of-control events accounted for 10% of reported UK general-aviation accidents and serious incidents.

rows.source: CAA loss-of-control-in-flight prevention
rows.verified: The same event class accounted for 38% of fatal general-aviation accidents in that period.

rows.source: CAA loss-of-control-in-flight prevention
rows.verified: Loss-of-control events accounted for 19% of serious-injury general-aviation accidents in that period.

rows.source: CAA loss-of-control-in-flight prevention
rows.verified: CAA's Stay in Control campaign provides prevention guidance for general-aviation pilots.

rows.source: CAA loss-of-control-in-flight prevention
rows.verified: CAA guidance addresses loss-of-control hazards during take-off and landing.

rows.source: CAA loss-of-control-in-flight prevention
rows.verified: CAA guidance addresses loss-of-control hazards in the circuit.

rows.source: CAA loss-of-control-in-flight prevention
rows.verified: CAA safety information highlights aircraft-state awareness, technical competence and startle effects during multiple system malfunctions.

rows.source: CAA loss-of-control-in-flight prevention
rows.verified: Loss-of-control risk depends on aircraft type, flight phase, weather, pilot proficiency, angle of attack, systems, workload and startle response.

rows.source: CAA loss-of-control-in-flight prevention
rows.verified: CAA loss-of-control evidence is aircraft-, pilot-, operation-, environment-, event- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level accident probability.

rows.source: MCA cargo stowage and securing safety
rows.verified: MCA MGN 699 explains application of SOLAS Chapter VI and the Merchant Shipping (Carriage of Cargoes) Regulations 2024.

rows.source: MCA cargo stowage and securing safety
rows.verified: Cargo must be packed and secured to prevent damage or danger to the ship and people throughout the voyage.

rows.source: MCA cargo stowage and securing safety
rows.verified: Cargoes and cargo units must be loaded, stowed and secured in accordance with the approved Cargo Securing Manual.

rows.source: MCA cargo stowage and securing safety
rows.verified: The ship operator and master retain responsibility for ensuring cargo units are safely secured.

rows.source: MCA cargo stowage and securing safety
rows.verified: A Cargo Securing Manual should be easy to use and directly applicable to the individual ship.

rows.source: MCA cargo stowage and securing safety
rows.verified: Ships subject to SOLAS Chapter VI should carry relevant and current cargo-stowage and securing documentation.

rows.source: MCA cargo stowage and securing safety
rows.verified: Ro-ro vehicle stowage and securing procedures are intended to reduce risks to people and ships.

rows.source: MCA cargo stowage and securing safety
rows.verified: Existing containerships must meet applicable design and operational requirements of the CSS Code as far as practicable.

rows.source: MCA cargo stowage and securing safety
rows.verified: Cargo-securing risk depends on cargo type, mass, packaging, ship design, securing equipment, voyage conditions, procedures and crew competence.

rows.source: MCA cargo stowage and securing safety
rows.verified: MCA cargo evidence is ship-, cargo-, voyage-, manual-, operation- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level maritime-incident probability.
